title: Beyond the Next Fold: CP2Seq, an Origami Benchmark for Long-Horizon Planning with Executable Verification
content: We introduce CP2Seq, a benchmark of 600 generated instances in which a model receives a crease pattern and a target folded stack and must build an executable fold sequence from an unfolded square. The environment checks every action, and terminal success is decided on creases, layer order and original-sheet region identity under stated numerical tolerances. Our central finding is that the models' directed choices do worse than undirected sampling in the same action space. Given the exact coordinates, orientations and stacking of every layer, a legality check on each action, enumeration of every legal action and automatic target comparison, Luna models solve 50 of 360 ablation cases and solve none of the 90 medium and 90 hard cases. On the same instances and the same legal action set, random legal folding succeeds in 57% of easy and 96% of some-layers episodes, against 50% and 80% for the best Luna condition, and breadth-first search solves 5/10 medium instances within 10^5 expansions. Matched controls locate the gap. It is not reachability, because search solves these targets. It is not perception: removing images while keeping exact numeric layer descriptions leaves solve rate unchanged (3/40 against 2/40). It is not stopping: an oracle stop at the first matching state adds two solves across 143 episodes. It is search bookkeeping: tracking which states have been tried and which branches are still open. Models visit 0.11-0.25 of the distinct states random folding covers, and in 71/104 full restarts they abandon a position three removed folds from a repair. Raising reasoning effort (8/120 to 26/120) and adding tools (6/40 to 11/40) both help without closing the gap, so what is missing is an external search frontier rather than a better next-action choice. The ordering holds for a second model family: on the shared 20 instances Sonnet solves 14/20 in one episode each, against a random expectation of 15.3/20 and a Luna single-trial median of 9/20, a smaller shortfall than Luna's but still no advantage over sampling. Verifier semantics decide these numbers. Our original plane-only comparator admitted 22 false successes among 536 accepted episodes, and five identical Luna trials spread 4/20, which bounds what single-run comparisons at this size can establish. These ablations cover 40 of the 600 instances and two model families, and cycling terminates 191 of 305 unsuccessful completed episodes, which we report as a protocol label and not a cause. We release the generator, environment, verifier and harness so that the located behavior can be measured under controlled intervention.
